notes: The contract maps the portable periodic HLAlookahead case directly to the pinned 2025 MIM and public C++ API clauses. Installed-package results are bounded provider evidence, not proof of provider-independent behavior or conformance.

requirements.statement: The standard MIM declares HLAlookahead as a periodic HLAtimeInterval controlled by HLAsetTiming.HLAreportPeriod, defines it as the minimum future duration for TSO scheduling, and leaves it undefined when the represented federate is not time-regulating. HLAsetTiming specifies the report period in seconds and a zero period stops periodic updates; HLAtimeInterval is the MIM's variable-length byte representation of an encoded logical-time interval. The scenario enables time regulation with the adapter-selected factory epsilon, requests a one-second reporting period, decodes the reported interval with the selected standard LogicalTimeFactory, and checks periodic reports against Query Lookahead both before and after an increased Modify Lookahead value.
The subject enters the standard regulating role with the adapter-selected logical-time factory's epsilon interval before relying on the MIM lookahead value.
After Enable Time Regulation, the subject services callbacks until exactly one timeRegulationEnabled callback is observed before the periodic MIM report is interpreted.

The regulating subject raises its lookahead to a distinct standard interval and queries the current value; the monitor then verifies a later periodic HLAlookahead reflection encodes that same interval.
The test obtains the enabled and modified service-side lookahead values through Query Lookahead and uses those standard interval encodings as the expected HLAlookahead reports.
The monitor uses the standard Send Interaction service and standard-encoded HLAfederate/HLAreportPeriod MIM parameters to start periodic reporting and sets the period to zero for cleanup.
